Based on the bug report and your provided snippets, the root cause is that when you switch between parallel and sequential multi‐instance on a subprocess (or task), the `loopCharacteristics` from the **target** (i.e. the new desired multi‐instance definition) are never applied, because in `BpmnReplace` only a small whitelist of “custom” properties get picked from the `target`. All other properties, including `loopCharacteristics`, are either copied from the old element or dropped, but never taken from the new `target`.  

The minimal fix is to add `loopCharacteristics` into the `CUSTOM_PROPERTIES` array in **lib/features/replace/BpmnReplace.js** so that your replace‐with‐sequential‐multi‐instance or replace‐with‐parallel‐multi‐instance options (which already supply `target.loopCharacteristics`) will actually be assigned onto the new business object.  

Here is the one *SEARCH/REPLACE* patch:

```javascript
### lib/features/replace/BpmnReplace.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
var CUSTOM_PROPERTIES = [
  'cancelActivity',
  'instantiate',
  'eventGatewayType',
  'triggeredByEvent',
  'isInterrupting'
];
=======
var CUSTOM_PROPERTIES = [
  'cancelActivity',
  'instantiate',
  'eventGatewayType',
  'loopCharacteristics',    // ← add this so that new multi‐instance settings stick
  'triggeredByEvent',
  'isInterrupting'
];
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With this change, whenever you invoke the replace action that carries a `target.loopCharacteristics` (e.g. sequential vs. parallel multi‐instance), that entire object is picked up and assigned to the new element, and so your multi‐instance properties will no longer be lost.
